static_traits.name: Li Cheng
static_traits.social_status: Having one close friend to confide in, but not yet sharing current distress; interactions with potential romantic partners affected by low self-worth
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; never received psychotherapy/counseling in the past
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, high cooperativeness, able to identify and describe automatic thoughts; tending to ignore positive feedback and replace it with dismissive explanations; steady emotional tone, willing to reflect

basic_info.main_problem: I feel I lack cheerfulness; men may find me unlovable, which makes me feel unworthy and very lonely.
basic_info.core_demands: I want to improve my self-esteem and stop feeling so unworthy; I hope to see myself from a better perspective and no longer be overly affected by these negative thoughts.
growth_experiences: Experiences of repeated romantic failures and rejections, especially after the most recent breakup (starting about 6 months ago) negative feelings have significantly intensified, with persistent 'unworthy and lonely' feelings repeatedly activated when socializing or meeting new friends.
Similar feelings of worthlessness and loneliness appeared after each previous breakup, but I never sought professional help before; no significant physical illness history.

core_beliefs: I am not worthy of being loved
I have no attractiveness / I am not good enough

special_situations.event: When socializing or meeting new friends (e.g. dates, parties)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am not cheerful enough or interesting enough, others will not like me / will not love me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Deliberately changes appearance and forces oneself to be more outgoing to please others
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will find me unlovable / no one will like me

special_situations.event: When feedback after a date is unclear or there are small mistakes
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Any small thing going wrong means total failure and proves I am unlovable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Afterwards repeatedly ruminates on experiences and jumps to conclusions to lower expectations
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: We will never meet again; I may be destined to be alone

special_situations.event: When receiving positive evaluations or affirmation from friends or colleagues
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Others' affirmation is unreliable, often just polite words
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignores or devalues positive evidence to maintain existing views
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are just being polite when saying nice things

special_situations.event: When recalling past breakups or rejection experiences
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Past failures prove I am essentially unlovable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Lowering expectations and reducing self-exposure to avoid being hurt again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I was never worthy of being liked

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be loved and accepted, to build a stable and mutually appreciating intimate relationship
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being rejected, being dismissed, and being abandoned after exposing 'not good enough / unlovable'
defense_goal: Reducing the hurt of being rejected through preemptive Self-denial and lowered expectations
Maintaining psychological distance to avoid vulnerability and shame in intimacy

object_relations.self_representation: Unloved, a rejected person of insufficient worth
object_relations.object_representation: Picky judges or potential rejecters (especially potential intimate partners)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the other person is silent, has a neutral expression, or gives unclear feedback in social or dating situations
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The other person is judging me like past rejecters did (they find me boring/unlovable)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Stating others' thoughts in hypothetical sentences (such as 'they must think...'), with a hesitant tone, avoiding directly inquiring into the facts.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When receiving positive feedback, praise, or expressions of willingness to meet again from others
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: This is just politeness or perfunctoriness, not genuine affirmation of me
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using explanations like 'they are just being polite / saying pleasantries' to dilute positive information, in a restrained tone, quickly shifting the topic.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked whether one has sought help from close friends or expressed vulnerability
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Expressing needs will trouble others and lead to being disliked / rejected
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Avoiding emotional expression with rational reasons (not wanting to trouble others), in a rational and objective tone, reducing emotional vocabulary.

manifestations: Persistently feeling lonely and unneeded after the breakup
Firmly believing 'no one will love me' in social and dating situations
Not seeking help from close friends, choosing to bear it alone
outcomes: Avoiding accepting support leading to deepened isolation
Developing negative anticipation and anxiety about building relationships

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths.
manifestations: Treats 'I should be cheerful / outgoing to be loved' as a self-standard
Tries changing appearance and forcing extroversion to please others

contact_model.definition: The individual turns the energy of the original desire directed outward toward himself, suppressing the impulse to express outwardly or seek help.
manifestations: Knowing there are close friends yet not seeking help, believing 'do not trouble others'
Pushes the impulse to need support back into oneself, bearing emotions alone

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact.
manifestations: Treats positive evaluations as 'just politeness', avoiding directly accepting affirmation
Quickly shifting attention away when receiving positive signals, not engaging with positive experiences

exception_events.target_problem: After dates or socializing, the client usually automatically thinks 'no one will love me', feels markedly low, and views relationship prospects through negative conclusions.
exception_events.unique_outcome: On one dinner date, the other party said they 'enjoyed the conversation' and proactively suggested meeting again; the conversation was smooth at the time, the whole date was completed successfully, and positive cues contrary to previous beliefs appeared.
exception_events.reason: Cues: the setting was a one-on-one dinner with smooth conversation; the other person gave direct positive feedback (suggesting meeting again); despite being nervous, the client kept participating in the conversation.

positive_force: Having stable work, occupational functioning not yet affected
Has one close friend who can provide potential support
Willing to seek help and change, with a positive attitude
Able to identify automatic thoughts and try forming more balanced statements
In real dating situations, can unfold and maintain high-quality conversations
negative_force: Core low sense of self-worth, tending toward Self-denial
Marked cognitive biases such as mind reading, predicting the future, and mental filtering
Dismissing positive information, finding it hard to internalize positive feedback
Avoiding seeking support for fear of troubling others; insufficient use of social support
Rigidly binds 'cheerful/outgoing' with 'being loved' (condition of worth)

target_behavior.behavior: Developing intense self-deprecation and negative self-talk of 'destined to be unloved' after socializing/dating, accompanied by low mood and loneliness
antecedent: Small mistakes during interaction or receiving unclear feedback
Being alone and ruminating after the activity
target_behavior.core_reason: Repeated breakup/rejection experiences reinforcing the belief 'I am not worthy of being loved', maintained through biases such as mind reading, predicting the future, and mental filtering
target_behavior.function: Avoiding the anxiety and uncertainty of being rejected again in the short term by lowering expectations
target_behavior.consequence: Long-term impaired self-esteem, intensified loneliness, blocked intimate relationship building, decreased interests and daily pleasures

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids expressing distress to close friends and seeking support (self-isolation)
antecedent: Thinking of seeking help when in low mood or feeling frustrated after socializing
When the thought of worrying about 'troubling others' appears
target_behavior.core_reason: Fearing that exposing vulnerability leads to rejection or disgust, repressing the urge to seek help with rational reasons
target_behavior.function: Avoids the potential risks of shame and rejection, maintaining a surface sense of control
target_behavior.consequence: Lack of social support, prolonged negative emotions, deepened isolation and helplessness
